newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs rebound from lows, close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs rebound from lows, close slightly lower.

text.p: Expectations of stronger cash hog markets next week offset pressure from Japan's denial it was considering cutting a pork import tariff, and CME hog futures closed slightly lower in most months, traders said.

Hogs ended 0.750 cent per lb lower to 0.050 higher with April hogs off 0.350 at 73.625 cents. June rallied 1.400 cent from its early low and ended 0.400 lower. Only August closed up after setting a high of 79.900 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.775 to 0.425 cent lower. May was off 0.775 at 79.400 cents.
Ideas cash hogs will show a firmer tone next week offset much of the early selling on the Japan denial.
"The product (market) has firmed up a bit and packer demand for hogs Monday should be a least steady," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.

Levitt also noted that although hog futures have shown wide price swings on speculation over how and if Japan will fill a void in meat imports following the Taiwan pork ban, the Taiwan ban overall remains a supporting factor.

Somebody will have to make up for the five to six million hogs that Taiwan is not going to be exporting the product from and the U.S. is looking at pork production being the same as last year during the final two quarters, he noted.

If the U.S. picks up only half of the Taiwan business, about 2.5 million hogs worth, U.S. packers would need a three-percent increase in total slaughter this year to meet that demand. This would be very hard to to do when the last Hogs and Pigs report indicated hog production the second half of this year being only unchanged from last year, Levitt said.

A sharp early break in hog futures came on Japan's denial that it was planning to cut its tariff on pork early due to rising pork prices. The denial came one day after a Japanese government official said it was considering cutting the tariff early--news that boosted hog futures to limit gains Thursday.

LFG was a notable buyer of June hogs on the rally, traders said. Cargill Investor Services and Rand Financials bought June and July while ABN Chicogo Corp sold. In hog options, commission houses sold June 76 puts and April 74 calls while buying October 70 puts, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures followed price swings in hog futures but held much of their early loss on expectations that bellies will not benefit as much from the Taiwan pork ban as other pork cuts will. Some traders expect the cash product market topping after again reaching the $75 per cwt level. Slicer interest had been good but could slip, they said.
Rosenthal Collins sold late while Refco and E.D.&F. Man bought. LIT division of First Options sold May early while RBH bought, pit sources said.

The new fresh belly contract posted its initial trade shortly after 1000 CST when LIT division of First Options bought five November 1998 contracts at 60.000 from R.J. O'Brien. November was then offered down to 44.000 cents by the close.
